Zod schemas have no custom toString, so both computed keys evaluate to the string "[object Object]", and duplicate keys collapse — the schema effectively only validates/strips to access_token. Then the code does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` and callers (e.g., GoogleCalendarService storing the parsed key back to the credential) would persist a key

Zod schemas have no custom toString, so both computed keys evaluate to the string "[object Object]", and duplicate keys collapse — the schema effectively only validates/strips to access_token. Then the code does `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` and callers (e.g., GoogleCalendarService storing the parsed key back to the credential) would persist a key missing refresh_token/expiry. Also `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a zod safeParse result (not data) while GoogleCalendarService uses it directly as `key`, compounding the breakage. Verifiable directly from the diff.

judged_text: minimumTokenResponseSchema (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11) is broken: the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to the literal '[object Object]' (Zod schemas don't implement toString; the duplicate key collapses to the second), so the 'minimum' schema validates/keeps only access_token and z.object's default strip discards everything else.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), [z.string().toString()]: z.number(), [z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional() })`. Those computed property names evaluate to a single concrete string at runtime (whatever `.toString()` returns for the Zod schema objects), not “any key”. This does not create a catch-all schema; instead it defines (at most) one or two fixed keys, and `z.object` will strip all other unknown properties by default. So when the “minimum” path is taken, fields like `expiry_date` (and any other token fields) will be discarded from the parsed output, defeating the intent of accepting/keeping arbitrary token response properties.
